issues.description: The template's StockIngredient class defines the quantity accessor as retrieveQuantity(), but the Stock class (in the template) calls getQuantity(), and the problem statement requires standard getters for private fields. This name mismatch prevents the template from compiling and conflicts with the UML / solution which use getQuantity().
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the quantity accessor in the template StockIngredient from retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() (returning int) so it matches the problem statement expectation, the Stock class usage, and the solution. Alternatively, update Stock.java to call retrieveQuantity(), but aligning to getQuantity() is recommended to match the UML and provided solution.

issues.description: The template introduces a quantity getter named retrieveQuantity() in StockIngredient, while the problem statement expects standard getters and the solution uses getQuantity(). Stock.java in the template calls getQuantity(), creating a naming mismatch that prevents students from mapping the 'quantity' getter requirement to the provided code and causes compilation/confusion. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual getter (quantity) across artifacts impedes straightforward mapping from the problem to the template and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template's retrieveQuantity() method to getQuantity() (keeping its behavior) so the StockIngredient getter follows the standard getX convention used in the problem statement and solution. Alternatively, update all callers to use retrieveQuantity(), but the preferred fix is to align on getQuantity() to match the solution and the explicit getter expectation.
